title: K12Vista: Exploring the Boundaries of MLLMs in K-12 Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the limited availability of comprehensive benchmarks for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on K-12 educational tasks, especially in Chinese science subjects. The authors argue that prior benchmarks are too narrow in subject coverage, data scale, question-type diversity, and evaluation methodology, often focusing only on final-answer accuracy rather than the reasoning process.

To address this, the paper introduces K12Vista, a large Chinese multimodal benchmark with 33,660 questions spanning five subjects (mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, and geography) across K-12 grade levels and three question types: multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, and free-response. The benchmark includes rich metadata such as grade, knowledge points, difficulty, and reference solution steps. The paper also proposes a process-evaluation pipeline, including K12-PEM-800K for step-level supervision and K12-PEM for judging reasoning quality, along with K12-PEBench for human-annotated evaluation of process assessment.

The context is benchmark development and model evaluation rather than a classroom intervention. The paper evaluates multiple closed- and open-source MLLMs, finding that reasoning-enhanced models such as Gemini2-thinking perform best, while all models struggle more with higher-grade problems, fill-in-blank items, and free-response reasoning. The main conclusion is that current MLLMs have substantial weaknesses in K-12 multimodal reasoning, and that step-by-step evaluation reveals errors and limitations that answer-only scoring misses.

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google multimodal large language model family used for reasoning and evaluation tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as one of the expert models for step-wise annotation in K12-PEM-800K construction, as a baseline MLLM on K12Vista, and in examples such as Gemini2-thinking and Gemini2-flash.

findings.finding_summary: On K12Vista, Gemini2-thinking achieved the highest reported overall accuracy among the listed MLLMs. It scored 55.47% on direct inference and 57.36% on step-by-step evaluation across the full benchmark; the paper also reports that reasoning-enhanced models like Gemini2-thinking performed better than most others.
findings.measure: Accuracy on K12Vista direct inference and step-by-step evaluation

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT model family used for multimodal reasoning and evaluation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in the paper as GPT-4o for solution generation, step decomposition, expert panel judging, caption extraction, and direct-inference evaluation.

findings.finding_summary: GPT-4o was used as part of the expert panel and as an evaluation model, with the paper reporting a kappa coefficient of 0.91 for direct-score evaluation and 0.73 for step-by-step evaluation against expert averages. In benchmark performance, GPT-4o scored 35.02% overall on direct inference and 35.00% overall on step-by-step evaluation on K12Vista.
findings.measure: Kappa coefficient vs expert evaluations; accuracy on K12Vista
findings.sample_size: n=1,000 sampled for quality assessment; n=33,660 questions for benchmark accuracy

identified_tools.name: Qwen
identified_tools.description: Alibaba Qwen multimodal and language model family used for generation, captioning, evaluation, and process supervision.
identified_tools.use_case: Used for data cleaning, caption generation, direct inference evaluation (Qwen2.5-VL-72B), process evaluation model fine-tuning (K12-PEM based on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct), and as a baseline across multiple model sizes.

findings.finding_summary: The paper reports that Qwen2.5-VL-72B achieved 51.39% direct-inference overall accuracy and 49.93% step-by-step overall accuracy on K12Vista, while Qwen2.5-VL-32B reached 55.42% and 53.35% respectively. For evaluation reliability, Qwen2.5-VL-72B had a kappa of 0.88 on direct-score evaluation and 0.67 on step-by-step evaluation against expert averages.
findings.measure: Accuracy on K12Vista; kappa coefficient vs expert evaluations
findings.sample_size: n=33,660 questions; n=1,000 sampled for quality assessment

identified_tools.name: DeepSeek
identified_tools.description: DeepSeek language model family used in the study as a text-only baseline after image captioning.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as a text-only LLM using captions generated from images and concatenated with questions.

findings.finding_summary: Deepseek-v3 was evaluated in the text-plus-caption setting and achieved 44.97% overall direct-inference accuracy and 47.60% overall step-by-step accuracy on K12Vista. The paper reports that text-only LLMs generally performed worse than top multimodal models, underscoring the importance of visual information.
findings.measure: Accuracy on K12Vista using captions plus text

quality_tier_rationale: This is an evaluation/benchmark paper rather than an intervention study, and it does not report experimental treatment effects in the K-12 classroom sense. The evidence is useful for model comparison but is not the type of causal educational evidence the tiering system rewards.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports substantial differences in benchmark accuracy across models, but these are task-performance metrics rather than educational outcome gains. The findings are informative for model capability assessment, yet classroom impact is indirect and not quantified.
